summary: A process or flow diagram laid out by the server: name the steps (with a status) and the arrows between them (with an optional label), and it places them in layers with few crossings, routes the arrows at right angles, runs top to bottom on a tall screen and left to right on a wide one, and shows the current step and a dot per step when the space is too small.

nodes.doc: The steps: [{"id": "review", "label": "Security review", "status": "active"}] or plain strings (the label is the id). status: ok (done, a tick), active (filled), failed (a cross), pending (muted), or a theme colour name (a ring). 3 to 12 steps read well on a phone

edges.doc: The arrows: ["a", "b"], ["a", "b", "label"], {"from", "to", "label", "status"} or a chain string "a > b > c". Loops are fine (an arrow back up, e.g. a rejected branch returning to an earlier step). Keep labels to one or two short words

direction.doc: Leave it auto: it picks top-to-bottom or left-to-right from the space at run time. down / right are preferences, kept while they fit (they flip when the other way fits much better); down! / right! pin it whatever the screen

edgeStyle.doc: Right-angled arrows, or S-curves between layers (costs about 150 B more per arrow)

width.doc: Leave it out: it fills the window's width and adapts. An expression ("windowWidth() - 32") when it shares the width with something. A number is a most, not a size: it never asks for more than the window

height.doc: Leave it out: it fills the window's height and adapts. Under a title pass what is left ("windowHeight() - 64"). A number is a most, not a size

fontSize.doc: Step label size at full scale; it shrinks to 77% when space is tight and grows to 120% when there is plenty

summary.doc: Below about 40% of a comfortable size, show "Step 3 of 7", the current step and a dot per step instead of an unreadable diagram. false keeps the diagram

description.doc: Spoken summary of the whole diagram (each step's label is read anyway, with its status)

current.doc: The current step, so statuses follow the app: "@step" (a host variable holding the 0-based index in nodes), an expression, a number or a node id. Steps the current one can be reached from show done, the current one active, the rest pending (a branch not taken stays pending); -1 is before the first, the count is all done. Steps given failed or a theme colour keep it. Leave out to use the static statuses

background.doc: Its own background, so it reads in every look as the whole document; "@colors.surface" inside a card, "none" for the parent's

pitfalls: Leave width and height out: it fills the window and adapts (orientation, scale, summary). Under a title or inside padding pass what is left as an expression ("windowHeight() - 64"); numbers are only upper bounds, so a size written for one screen still fits a smaller one
Leave direction auto unless the shape of the screen is known; right and down are only preferences, right! and down! pin it and can leave too little room
Labels wrap to two lines (three when every label is long and the flow is short) and then end in an ellipsis: keep step names under about 30 characters
Edge labels sit beside the arrow just after its start: one or two words. Two labelled arrows leaving one step go out of separate ports so their labels part
A process deeper than about 7 steps does not fit a landscape phone: it shows the summary there. Pin direction only if you know the shape of the screen
Each node is a text box (measured, checked), arrows are one canvas: about 200 B per step and 100 B per arrow

current reads an index into nodes: a host variable declared in resources (e.g. {"variables": {"currentStep": {"value": 1, "export": true}}}) and passed as "@currentStep" (never name it step: that hides the step() function). Each step that follows it costs three faces, about 3x a static step
